text:
Dubai registered 10,419 residential sales valued at AED 27,337,275,204 in the last four weeks, a 4.4 percent decrease in volume from the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 3,889, which are recorded separately from sales transactions. The market continues to be dominated by off-plan transactions, which accounted for 65.4 percent of the total sales volume during this period.

The median residential price per square foot stood at AED 1,676, representing a 1.9 percent decline compared to the previous four weeks. Top performing areas by sales volume include Dubai South with 4,595 transactions and Down Town Jabal Ali with 2,518. In Dubai South, the median price per square foot was AED 1,705, while Down Town Jabal Ali recorded AED 1,732. Business Bay showed a median of AED 2,100 per square foot, reflecting its premium positioning relative to other major residential communities.

Rental activity remained robust with 81,118 Ejari contracts registered, where 50.5 percent were renewals. The median residential rent was AED 70,900 per year. Estimated gross yields are highest in International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent for flats, followed by Town Square at 7.0 percent. Dubai Studio City and Dubai Sports City both recorded estimated yields of 6.5 percent, while Dubai Production City followed at 6.4 percent for flat units.

Price momentum is diverging across communities. Al Yufrah 1 saw the strongest 12 week price increase at 35.9 percent, followed by Damac Hills at 16.6 percent. Conversely, Palm Deira experienced the sharpest decline at 18.0 percent, with Wadi Al Safa 7 down 14.1 percent. The anomaly monitor flagged 1,004 sales in the last 60 days that deviated significantly from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
